note_sections.t: Re-evaluation for prior prostate cancer diagnosis to discuss treatment options.

58-year-old male with a history of prostate adenocarcinoma diagnosed on biopsy. He owns a small cafe and cycles approximately 30 km three times per week. He is divorced and lives with his partner, with a long-time friend acting as his next of kin. He consumes about 3 units of alcohol weekly and is a current smoker with a 36 pack-year history. He has recently attended appointments for thyroid screening, suspected obstructive sleep apnoea, and baseline memory screening. His PSA has risen from 1.9 ng/mL in February 2024 to 2.4 ng/mL in February 2025. He reports moderate lower urinary tract symptoms with an IPSS score of 16/35.
On DRE, the prostate is normal in consistency and size, corresponding to clinical stage cT1c. General examination is unremarkable with a blood pressure of 128/76 mmHg and a heart rate of 45 bpm.
